'''Carborundum Universal Ltd''' ('''CUMI''') is an Indian company which manufactures and develops [[abrasive]]s, [[Ceramic material|ceramics]], [[Refractory|refractories]], aluminium oxide grains, [[machine tools]], [[polymers]], [[adhesives]] and [[mineral|electro minerals]] in India.<ref>{{cite book | last = LastName | first = FirstName | title = India business yearbook, 2009 | publisher = Vikas Pub. House Distributors, UBS Publishers' Distributors | location = Noida, UP New Delhi | year = 2009 | isbn = 9788125930860 }} Pg. No: 171</ref> It is a part of the [[Murugappa Group]].

The company has subsidiaries in India, Russia, South Africa, Australia, China, Thailand and Canada.

==History==
[[File:Cumi(1954).jpg|thumb|CUMI-1954]]
CUMI was established as a result of diversification from banking business through [[Bicycle|cycle]] manufacturing with the intent to manufacture [[abrasive|abrasive materials]]. CUMI's [[parent company]], the [[Murugappa Group]], made a tie up with Carborundum UK, a subsidiary of American abrasive manufacturer, [[Edward Goodrich Acheson|'''Carborundum''']] and the '''Universal Grinding Co. Ltd. UK''' in 1950. The result was the '''Carborundum Universal of Madras'''. Then it was renamed and incorporated in 1954 as Carborundum Universal Ltd (CUMI).<ref>{{cite book | last = Kazmi | first = Azhar | title = Strategic management and business policy | publisher = Tata McGraw Hill Education | location = New Delhi | year = 2008 | isbn = 9780070263628 }}Pg. No: 214</ref>

===Establishments===
Initially CUMI was founded to manufacture the core products for the collaborating companies. Later the company established its first [[bonded abrasive]] plant at [[Chennai]] with the facility acquired from Ajax Products and began its manufacturing in the abrasives platform. With the intention of producing [[ceramic material|technical ceramics]] for high temperature insulation products CUMI has made joint venture with [[Morgan Crucible]] Plc. UK resulted in the establishment of Murugappa Morgan Thermal Ceramics Ltd in 1982.<ref name="Murugappa Morgan">{{cite web|url=http://www.murugappamorgan.com/|title= Murugappa Morgan}}</ref>

The company has laid a strong foundation in [[ceramic material|engineered ceramics]] through number of joint ventures. In 1991 Wendt (India) Ltd, a joint ventured company of Wendt GmbH, Germany and The House of Khataus, was merged with the CUMI.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-03-09/news/31139854_1_winterthur-technologies-carborundum-universal-murugappa|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305021538/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-03-09/news/31139854_1_winterthur-technologies-carborundum-universal-murugappa|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 March 2016|title=Murugappa group-3M battle over Wendt India enters new phase|publisher=The Economic Times-Bennett, Coleman & Co. Ltd.|date= 9 March 2012}}</ref> CUMI's first [[ceramic material|industrial ceramics]] division was established in [[Hosur]], [[Tamil Nadu]] as a technical partnership with [[Coors Ceramics]], USA in 1991.<ref>{{cite book | last = Rao | first = B. V. S. | title = Ceramic powders for high-tech applications | publisher = Universities Press distributor Sangam | location = Hyderabad London | year = 1995 | isbn = 0863115608| page= 104 }}</ref> Later it was expanded with the unique Metallized Cylinders Plant.

As a part of expanding their presence, in 2005 the company started CUMI Middle East FZE in Ras Al Khaimah. In order to strengthen their global presence CUMI bought Abrasive Enterprises Inc., Canada, for $2.24 Million by 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/abrasive-enterprises-sold-1.570668 |title= Abrasive Enterprises sold |publisher= CBC/Radio-Canada|date= 2 March 2006 }}</ref> After a year CUMI established CUMI International Ltd in Cyprus.

===Acquisitions===
Within a decade, after the withdrawal of the collaborators, CUMI acquired Ajax Products Pvt Ltd. CUMI stepped up its investment in abrasive industries by acquiring the Eastern Abrasives Ltd., [[Kolkata]] in 1978. In 1997, Cutfast Abrasive Tools Ltd., Eastern Abrasives Ltd., Cutfast Polymers Ltd. and Carborundum Universal Investment merged with Carborundum Universal Ltd.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://expressindia.indianexpress.com/fe/daily/19971217/35155103.html|title=Cutfast Abrasives merges with CUMI|publisher=The Indian Express|date=17 December 1997|access-date=1 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305051750/http://expressindia.indianexpress.com/fe/daily/19971217/35155103.html|archive-date=5 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Within a year of acquisition of Sterling Abrasives Ltd. and SEDCO in 2003, CUMI acquired CUMI Australia Pty Ltd. In 2007 the company took over the Chinese firm, Sanhe Yanjiao Jingri Diamond Industrial Company Ltd., and the Russian Volzhsky Abrasive Works.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2013-07-19/news/40681613_1_vellayan-dabur-ceo-sunil-duggal|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130722212602/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2013-07-19/news/40681613_1_vellayan-dabur-ceo-sunil-duggal|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 July 2013|title=The Economic Times |publisher=Bennett, Coleman & Co. Ltd.|date=19 July 2013}}</ref> Further acquisitions followed in 2008, including Foskor Zirconia Ltd., South Africa which became a subsidiary of CUMI.<ref>{{cite book | last = Survey | first = Geological | title = Minerals Yearbook 2008 Metals and Minerals | publisher = Government Printing Office | location = US | year = 2011 | isbn = 9781411330153 }} Pg.No: 85-3</ref>

===Diversification===
Besides manufacturing, marketing and distribution, CUMI is also involved in diversified works like [[mining]], [[Electricity generation|power generation]] and [[Technology transfer|TOT]] agreements with various organizations.

CUMI acquired [[Bauxite]] mines at Bhatia and [[Okha, India|Okha]] in Gujarat, a Silicon Carbide plant in [[Koratty]], Kerala and a brown Aluminium Oxide grains plant at [[Edapally]], Kerala. CUMI established a 12MW [[hydroelectricity|hydroelectric power plant]] at [[Maniyar]], Kerala in 1994.<ref>{{cite book | last = Honningsvåg | first = Bjørn | title = Hydropower in the new millennium : proceedings of the 4th International Conference on Hydropower Development, Hydropower '01, Bergen, Norway, 20-22 June 2001 | publisher = A.A. Balkema | location = Lisse, Netherlands Exton (PA | year = 2001 | isbn = 9789058091956 }}Pg. no: 223</ref> and a 5.5MW Wind mill at Nallur.

CUMI made a [[technology transfer]] with Answer Technology Inc., USA for advanced monolithics and a technical collaboration with [[National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology]] of India, [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] of India and [[Pennsylvania State University]] of USA for the development of advanced ceramic technology.

'''CUMI Direct'''

CUMI Direct is an online e-commerce platform that was started in 2005 and sells:

* [[Material-handling equipment|Warehouse Equipment]] - Pallet Trucks, Stackers, Table Lifts, Movable Dock Ramps, Stationary Dock Levelers, Tail Lifts, Fork Lifts, Plastic Pallets, Caster Wheels
* [[Material-handling equipment|Material Handling Equipment]] - Shopping Trolleys, Hand Carts
* [[Power tool|Power Tools]] - CUMI Power Tools, METABO Power Tools
* [[Industrial Ceramics]]
* Electro Minerals
* [[Abrasives]] - Thin Wheels, Rolls, Grinding Wheels, Non Woven Wheels, Coated Abrasives, Porous Tiles, Super Abrasives, Resonoid and Rubber, Vitrified Ranges
* Metal Working Fluids - Cleaner, Forming Fluids, Neat Oils, Rust Preventives, Water Solubles
* [[Strapping|Strapping Tools]] - Tensioners, Sealers
* [[Refractory|Super Refractories products]] - Fired Refractories, Monolithic Products
Most of the products are granted CE and GS certificates.

==Product applications and materials==
[[File:Products IC.JPG|thumb|Advanced Ceramic Products]]

Carborundum Universal Ltd (CUMI) is an Indian company which manufactures and develops abrasives, ceramics, refractories, aluminium oxide grains, machine tools, polymers, adhesives and electro minerals in India. It is a part of the Murugappa Group.
The company has subsidiaries in India, Russia, South Africa, Australia, China, Thailand and Canada.
